speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. You've presented with blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me how long you've had these symptoms and if they are painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS). The combination of mucosal ulcers (mouth, genitalia), skin blisters, and recent initiation of captopril is highly suggestive of a severe cutaneous adverse reaction. I have made my diagnosis based on the clinical evidence provided.
